stem: The Radio Equipment Directive in this pack is:
explanation: The RED Guide opens on Directive 2014/53/EU and states that it applies from 13 June 2016. The EMC and low-voltage directives are related, but they are not the RED.

stem: Radio waves, for the RED, are electromagnetic waves:
choices: Of frequencies lower than 3 000 GHz, propagated in space without an artificial guide
explanation: Article 2 of the RED, as quoted in the Guide, uses 3 000 GHz and no artificial guide. The Guide notes that this idea includes near-field uses such as NFC.

stem: Radio equipment under the RED is an electrical or electronic product that:
choices: Any product with a clock above 9 kHz
Intentionally emits and/or receives radio waves for communication or radiodetermination, or must be completed with an accessory such as an antenna to do so
explanation: That is the Article 2 definition used in the Guide. A product that needs an antenna accessory to radiate on purpose is still radio equipment.

stem: The RED Guide treats which places as within the directive's geographic application, along with the EU?
choices: The United Kingdom as a Member State
EEA-EFTA states (Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway) and Türkiye
explanation: Section 1.2 says the Guide's words 'Member State' also cover those EEA-EFTA states and Türkiye. The UK is handled separately as a third country.

stem: Placing on the market means:
choices: The first time a user turns the product on
The first making available of each individual product on the Union market
Type approval of a design, once, for every future unit
explanation: Section 1.3 says placing on the market is per individual product, the first time it is made available, whether the unit was built alone or in a series.

stem: A radio shown at a trade fair is not treated as placed on the market when:
choices: A visible sign says it may not be made available or put into service until it conforms, and the demo controls interference and risk
The sign is only in the company's home country
The booth has no sign but the radio is CE marked in advance
Any powered demo is automatically compliant
explanation: Article 9.2, as set out in §1.6, requires that sign and adequate measures against interference, disturbance, and risk. A transmitter demo also means contacting the spectrum authority.

stem: Radio equipment in the scope of the RED is, for those aspects:
choices: Covered only by the Machinery Directive
Excluded from both the LVD and the EMCD, while the RED points back to their essential requirements
Required to carry a separate EMCD declaration for the same EMC requirement
explanation: Section 10.5 quotes Article 1.4 of the RED and Article 2.2 of the EMCD. The LVD and EMCD do not apply, but Article 3.1 refers to their essential requirements.

stem: Article 3.1(b) of the RED is the essential requirement for:
explanation: The Guide's conformity figure labels Article 3.1(b) as EMC, 3.1(a) as health and safety, 3.2 as radio, 3.3 as specific requirements, and 3.4 as the charger.

stem: Article 3.2 of the RED is about:
choices: Only the CE mark font size
Effective use of the radio spectrum and avoidance of harmful interference
explanation: Article 3.2 is the radio essential requirement. Directive 2013/35/EU is a worker-protection law and, per §10.6, is not listed on the EU declaration of conformity.

stem: For Articles 3.2 and 3.3, if the relevant harmonised standards are not applied in full or do not exist, the manufacturer uses:
choices: A supplier's declaration under FCC Part 15
Module B+C or Module H, both with a notified body
explanation: Section 2.8 says Module A stays available for 3.1(a), 3.1(b), and 3.4 even without a harmonised standard. For 3.2 and 3.3, partial or missing harmonised standards force B+C or H.

stem: Module A in Annex II of the RED is:
choices: Full quality assurance with a notified body
A factory inspection by a market surveillance authority
Internal production control, with no notified body
explanation: The Guide's figure shows Annex II as Module A without a notified body. Annex III is B+C and Annex IV is Module H, both with a notified body.

stem: A harmonised standard whose reference is in the Official Journal gives:
choices: A presumption of conformity for the essential requirements it covers
The right to skip the technical documentation
explanation: Section 2.8 says applying those standards is optional, and doing so brings the presumption of conformity for the corresponding requirements. It also changes which module is available for Articles 3.2 and 3.3.

stem: The EU declaration of conformity should declare:
choices: Compliance with the applicable EU legislation only
UKCA legislation in the same sentence as the CE claim
explanation: Section 1.2.5 says the DoC declares EU legislation. Other countries' declarations may sit separately, and section 10.6 says Directive 2013/35/EU does not belong on the DoC.

stem: Technical documentation and the EU declaration are kept available for:
choices: The life of the patent only
10 years after the radio equipment has been placed on the market
explanation: The Guide repeats the 10-year period for the manufacturer, the authorised representative, and the importer's copy of the declaration.

stem: An authorised representative's mandate must not include which manufacturer duties?
choices: Ensuring the design meets Article 3, carrying out the conformity assessment, and drawing up the technical documentation
explanation: Section 2.4 says the duties in §§2.8(a), 2.8(b), and 2.8(d) shall not be part of the mandate. The mandate does include keeping the DoC and technical file for 10 years and cooperating with authorities.

stem: The importer must, for 10 years:
choices: Sign the declaration as the manufacturer
Keep a copy of the EU declaration and make sure the technical documentation can be provided, without having to hold that file on the shelf
Keep the full design file in the importer's office in every case
Skip traceability if the manufacturer is outside the EU
explanation: Section 2.5(h), with the Blue Guide note quoted there, says the importer keeps the DoC copy and ensures the technical file can be made available. There is no general duty to hold a copy of the file.

stem: Before making radio equipment available, a distributor verifies, among other things, that:
choices: The distributor has performed Module B
The product bears the CE mark, is accompanied by instructions and safety information, and can operate in at least one Member State
The product was built in the distributor's own factory
The product has an FCC ID
explanation: Section 2.7 lists the distributor's checks, including CE, instructions, the one-Member-State condition, identification, and traceability. The distributor does not replace the manufacturer's conformity assessment.

stem: Instructions for radio equipment must include, where applicable:
choices: Frequency bands and the power used, plus accessories and software that affect conformity
explanation: Section 2.3(j) and the later instructions clause require bands, power, and the accessories and software that let the radio operate as intended. The manufacturer is the one who defines intended use.

stem: If restrictions on putting into service exist, Article 10(10) information on the packaging may be:
choices: Omitted when the radio is CE marked
A short statement or a pictogram, with the detail in the instructions
explanation: Section 2.8(i) describes Implementing Regulation (EU) 2017/1354: a visible statement or a pictogram, plus the actual restrictions in the instructions.

stem: On products placed on the EU market, the Article 10(10) country code for Northern Ireland restrictions is:
explanation: Section 2.8(i) says that from 1 January 2021 the abbreviation UK has no Article 10(10) meaning for the EEA, and Northern Ireland uses UK(NI).

stem: A software update makes the radio a substantially modified product when:
choices: The battery is replaced with the same type
It changes intended functions, radio interface, type, or performance in a way the first risk assessment did not foresee, the hazard or risk increases, and the product is made available
explanation: Section 1.5 sets those three conditions together. An update that does not affect compliance can stay in the maintenance category, like an ordinary repair.

stem: Dual-use radio that is sold for both civil and excluded state-security use:
choices: Does not fall under the public-security exclusion
explanation: Section 1.7.3.1 says the exclusion is for equipment used exclusively for those activities. The Guide's TETRA example stays in the RED because it is not exclusively for the excluded activities.

stem: Amateur radio kits for assembly and use by radio amateurs are:
choices: Covered by the Marine Equipment Directive
Class A digital devices under FCC Part 15 only
Regarded as not made available on the market, so the amateur exclusion can apply
explanation: Section 1.7.3.2 lists amateur kits, amateur-modified equipment, and amateur-built experimental equipment as not made available on the market. Regular commercial supply can still be making available.

stem: Marine radio that must be carried on SOLAS ships under Directive 2014/90/EU is:
choices: Automatically CE marked with no other mark
Excluded from the RED, and may also carry the wheel mark if it is under that directive
explanation: Section 1.7.3.3 excludes equipment in the Marine Equipment Directive. A product that meets both regimes carries both the CE mark and the wheel mark, and non-SOLAS marine radio can still be in the RED.

stem: Ground aviation radio equipment is:
choices: Covered only by the EMCD even when it is radio
Covered by the RED unless another exemption applies
explanation: Section 1.7.3.5 says ground aviation radio is in the RED unless another exemption applies. Equipment not intended for exclusive airborne use is one of the cases the aviation regulation does not pull out of the RED.

stem: A custom-built evaluation kit is outside the RED only when it is all of:
choices: A production radio with a test mode
Any FPGA board sold from a catalogue
Custom-built, an evaluation kit, destined for professionals, and used solely at R&D facilities for R&D
explanation: Section 1.7.3.6 requires every element. Catalogue lab gear, a generic evaluation board, and a free-programmable SDR black box are given as examples that do not get the exemption.

stem: EN 301 489-1 V2.2.3 does not set limits for:
choices: Antenna-port emissions and radiated emissions from the radio's own enclosure
Radiated immunity from 80 MHz to 6 GHz
explanation: Clause 1 and clause 8.1.1 leave antenna-port and radio-enclosure radiated emissions to the Article 3.2 radio standards. The EMC phenomena in the rest of the document still apply.

stem: Ancillary equipment tested separately to EN 301 489-1 for enclosure radiated emissions meets:
choices: EN 55032 Class B, or Class A if it is only for an industrial environment or a telecommunication centre
FCC §15.109 Class A in every case
explanation: Clause 8.2.3 sets Class B as the rule and Class A as the alternative for exclusive industrial or telecom-centre use. The method is EN 55032.

stem: During continuous EMC phenomena, EN 301 489-1 requires the radio to:
choices: Keep operating as intended, not transmit by mistake, not change operating state, and not change critical stored data
Ignore the criterion until the test ends
Reset and wait for a user
Drop the link and recover later
explanation: Clause 6.1 is the continuous-phenomena criterion. It is what radiated immunity and continuous RF tests are judged against.

stem: For transient phenomena, EN 301 489-1 allows the radio to:
choices: Transmit on a new frequency during the event
Be disturbed during the event, but not change mode or lose critical stored data, and to operate as intended afterwards
explanation: Clause 6.2 separates the moment of the transient from the behaviour after it. A special, narrower allowance exists for surges on a single outdoor symmetrical port.

stem: EN 301 489-1 Table 2 applies ESD to:
choices: Fixed use and portable use, not vehicle use
explanation: In Table 2, electrostatic discharge is applicable for fixed and portable use and not applicable for vehicle use. Vehicle DC ports get the ISO 7637-2 transients instead.

stem: The radiated-immunity test level in EN 301 489-1 clause 9.2 is:
choices: 3 V/m unmodulated, then 80% AM at 1 kHz, or 400 Hz if the wanted signal already uses 1 kHz
explanation: Clause 9.2.2 sets 3 V/m measured unmodulated, then amplitude modulation. The frequency range is 80 MHz to 6 000 MHz, with the exclusion band applied.

stem: ESD severities in EN 301 489-1 clause 9.3 are:
explanation: Clause 9.3.2 states those severities and points the rest of the method, including intermediate levels, to EN 61000-4-2. The performance criterion is the transient one.

stem: A channelized transmitter's exclusion band in EN 301 489-1 extends:
choices: The whole operating band in standby
250% of the channel width either side of the centre frequency, and is not used in standby
explanation: Clause 4.3.2.2 sets the 250% extension. Clause 4.3.2.1 says exclusion bands are not applied when a transmitter is measured in standby.

stem: Receiver exclusion bands are not applied when:
choices: Measuring emissions of a receiver or of the receiver part of a transceiver
explanation: Clause 4.3.3.1 says exclusion bands are not applied for receiver emission measurements. Immunity exclusion for a receiver is a different calculation, and n is 1 when this document is used alone.

stem: The wanted receive signal during EN 301 489-1 immunity tests is set no higher than:
choices: The maximum the generator can produce
40 dB above the minimum usable level
explanation: Clause 4.2.3 caps the wanted signal at 40 dB above minimum usable level. For radiated immunity that level is checked with the disturbance amplifiers on but not driven.

stem: DC power conducted emissions in EN 301 489-1 are required when the DC cable to a local DC network is:
choices: Any length, including a 10 cm jumper
explanation: Clause 8.3.1 uses 3 m as the split. A DC cable of 3 m or less that goes to a dedicated AC/DC supply is assessed at that supply's AC port instead.

stem: EN 301 489-1 Table 5 DC conducted limits from 0.15 MHz to 0.5 MHz are:
explanation: Table 5 lists 79 / 66 from 0.15 MHz to 0.5 MHz and 73 / 60 from 0.5 MHz to 30 MHz. If a quasi-peak reading already meets the average limit, the average measurement is unnecessary.

stem: AC mains harmonic-current limits in EN 301 489-1 for equipment up to 16 A per phase come from:
explanation: Clause 8.5 points input current up to and including 16 A per phase to EN 61000-3-2, and current above 16 A up to 75 A per phase to EN 61000-3-12.

stem: Flicker limits for equipment up to 16 A per phase with no conditional connection come from:
explanation: Clause 8.6 uses EN 61000-3-3 when no conditional connection is needed. Conditional connection, or current from above 16 A to 75 A, uses EN 61000-3-11.

stem: Vehicle supply transients in EN 301 489-1 use ISO 7637-2 pulses:
choices: 1, 2a, 2b, 3a, 3b, and 4, at immunity test level III, on 12 V and 24 V ports
explanation: Clause 9.6.2 lists those pulses at level III. Pulses 1, 2a, 2b, and 4 are applied 10 times; pulses 3a and 3b run for 20 minutes and use the continuous criterion.

stem: AC mains surge levels in EN 301 489-1 clause 9.8, outside telecom centres, are:
choices: 1 kV line-to-ground and 0.5 kV line-to-line in every building
2 kV line-to-ground and 1 kV line-to-line, 1.2/50 µs
explanation: Clause 9.8.2.3 sets 2 kV and 1 kV for ordinary AC mains ports. Telecom centres use 1 kV line-to-ground and 0.5 kV line-to-line, and the criterion is the transient one.

stem: EFT on the AC mains port in EN 301 489-1 is:
choices: 1 kV open-circuit at a 5 kHz repetition rate
explanation: Clause 9.4.2 sets 1 kV and 5 kHz on AC mains. Signal, control, and DC ports that can have cables longer than 3 m are 0.5 kV at 5 kHz, and xDSL is 0.5 kV at 100 kHz.

stem: Conducted RF immunity in EN 301 489-1 clause 9.5 is:
choices: 10 V rms from 150 kHz to 80 MHz
3 V rms unmodulated from 150 kHz to 80 MHz, then 80% AM
explanation: Clause 9.5.2 calls that severity level 2 of EN 61000-4-6. It applies to AC mains and to other cables that may be longer than 3 m, and it uses the continuous performance criterion.

stem: REDCA TGN 01's reminder about combining marks is:
choices: The host does not need a manufacturer
A module certificate covers every host
explanation: Section 5.1 states that the final radio product is a new product and prints the reminder CE + CE ≠ CE. The manufacturer who places that combination on the market owns the compliance.

stem: EMC tests on a radio module, by themselves:
choices: Replace the final product's Article 3.1(b) assessment
Cover the host's other functions automatically
Are optional once the module has any CE mark
Do not give confidence of EMC compliance of the final radio product
explanation: Section 5.2 says EMC of the final product needs its own assessment, which in most cases means full EMC testing. Safety of the module likewise does not carry the final product.

stem: A notified-body EU-type certificate for the module:
choices: Is not a certificate for the final radio product
Can be copied onto the host as the host's certificate
explanation: Section 6.2 says it is not possible to treat the module's EU-type certificate as the final product's certificate. The final manufacturer may use module radio data only with a documented risk assessment, and still may need its own notified body.

stem: If the module has no fixed antenna and the installer adds an antenna trace, the module maker must:
choices: Describe that antenna path in detail for the installer
Rely on the host's FCC ID
explanation: Section 6.1 requires the antenna assembly or trace to be described, and critical accessories belong on the declaration and in the installation instructions. Changing them means more assessment.

stem: A USB dongle or a card the user plugs in and can remove is, in TGN 01:
choices: Always a final radio product needing a new module certificate
Not treated as a module installation; each product is assessed for that interconnection as its intended use
explanation: Annex A.1.1 distinguishes a user-removable plug-in from a radio that is permanently installed in the host when the final system is placed on the market. The permanent case is treated as a module installation.

stem: Service, programming, and other ports that are not cabled in normal use are, for EN 301 489-1:
choices: Fitted with 3 m of extra cable in every case
Left unconnected for the EMC test
explanation: Clause 9.1 says those ports are not cabled for EMC testing. If a cable has to be added to exercise the product, it must not change the evaluation.

stem: An optical fibre with a non-conductive screen is, in EN 301 489-1:
choices: Not a port for the EMC tests
explanation: Clause 3.1 says that interface does not interact with the electromagnetic environment in the frequency range of the standard, so it is not a port. It may still be used to watch performance.

stem: The transmitter under test in EN 301 489-1 is exercised at:
choices: Its maximum rated RF output power
A level 40 dB below rated power
explanation: Clause 4.2.2 sets the wanted transmit signal to the maximum rated RF power. Monitoring equipment stays outside the test environment.

stem: Voltage dips in EN 301 489-1 clause 9.7 include:
choices: 0% residual for 0.5 cycle, 0% for 1 cycle, and 70% residual for 25 cycles at 50 Hz
explanation: Clause 9.7.2 lists those dips plus a 0% interruption for 250 cycles at 50 Hz. The 0% dips use the transient criterion, and a product with no battery backup may lose volatile data on the 70% dip and the interruption.

stem: A product placed on the market in Switzerland under the MRA is:
choices: Automatically placed on the EU market
Not, by that act, placed on the EU market
Exempt from RED if it has a CE mark
explanation: Section 1.2.3.1 says there is no customs union, so Swiss placement is not EU placement. The MRA does adapt several operator duties when the economic operator is in the EU or Switzerland.

stem: For products moving from Switzerland into the EU, Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 Article 4 still requires:
choices: An economic operator established in the EU
explanation: The Guide notes that, at the time it was written, the Swiss MRA had no adaptation for that market-surveillance duty. An EU economic operator is still required.

stem: The manufacturer must mark the radio so it can be identified by:
choices: Nothing, if the DoC has a model name
A type, batch, serial number, or other element
The notified body logo with no other mark
explanation: Section 2.3(g) and §2.8(g) require that identifier. If the radio is too small, it goes on the packaging or in an accompanying document.

stem: Name and address on the EU declaration:
choices: Replace the label on the product
Are optional if a distributor exists
Must be indelible in the same way as the CE mark
Do not, by themselves, satisfy the product traceability duty
explanation: Section 2.8(h) says the address on the DoC is not enough. Traceability has to be on the product, or on the packaging or accompanying document when the product cannot carry it, and it does not have to be indelible like the CE mark.

stem: Member States may restrict putting into service of otherwise compliant radio equipment for reasons of:
choices: Whether the manual is longer than ten pages
Spectrum efficiency, harmful interference, electromagnetic disturbances, or public health
explanation: Section 1.4 quotes Article 7. Compliance with the RED is the starting point, and a Member State may still restrict use for those listed reasons.

stem: AMRD group devices, in the Guide's treatment, are:
choices: Within the scope of the RED
explanation: Section 1.7.3.4 says autonomous maritime radio devices are in the RED. Group A devices also sit under older Commission decisions on AIS and non-SOLAS GMDSS.

stem: Presumption of conformity from EN 301 489-1 arises when:
choices: The document is cited in the Official Journal and the normative clauses that match the requirement are followed
The module has an FCC grant
The lab owns a paper copy, whether or not the OJ lists it
explanation: Annex A says that once the document is cited in the OJ, compliance with the normative clauses in Table A.1 confers a presumption of conformity within the document's scope. Several rows are conditional on the ports that exist.

stem: Broadcast receivers are:
choices: Excluded from the scope of EN 301 489-1
Exempt from the RED in every case
explanation: Clause 1 says the document covers radio equipment and associated ancillary equipment, excluding broadcast receivers. Other standards may apply instead, including other parts of the EN 301 489 series.

stem: Multi-radio equipment, as drawn in EN 301 489-1, means:
choices: Two or more radios of different technologies that may operate at the same time
A receiver with two antennas of the same radio
explanation: Clause 3.1 and Figure 1 use that meaning. Multi-standard radio, Figure 2, is the case where common active RF parts handle more than one technology at once.

stem: If a final-product manufacturer relies on the module's Article 3.2 data but cannot obtain the module file, REDCA TGN 01 says:
choices: The module maker may have to send the file straight to the market-surveillance authority or the notified body
The test lab invents the missing results
The host CE mark covers the gap
The final product can ship with no file
explanation: Section 6.2 puts the duty on the final manufacturer to have a path for that file. Without it, a notified body may be unable to issue the EU-type certificate.

stem: TGN 01 says installation instructions for a module should tell the installer that:
choices: Only the FCC label must be copied
No further test is ever required
The final radio product still needs its own assessment
Article 3.1(b) does not apply to hosts
explanation: Section 6.1 recommends that warning so an installer does not treat a module CE mark as permission to skip the final product. The instructions should also say which tests the final product needs.

stem: The RED Guide is:
choices: Guidance, and the directive text wins if they differ
explanation: The Guide is the Commission's reading aid. Where a quiz item cites it, the underlying duty is still the directive article the Guide is explaining.

stem: A consumer who buys a radio in a third country and carries it home for personal use has, by that act alone, placed it on the EU market.
explanation: Section 1.3 says that personal import is not placing on the market, though national law can still make the RED relevant. Own-use construction is treated the same way.

stem: The manufacturer may choose not to use harmonised standards.
explanation: Section 2.8 says the choice is free. Skipping them removes the presumption of conformity and, for Articles 3.2 and 3.3, brings in a notified body.

stem: Module A can be used for Article 3.1(b) even when the EMC harmonised standard is not applied.
explanation: The Guide is explicit that for 3.1(a), 3.1(b), and 3.4 the manufacturer may always use Module A. A notified body is not required for that choice.

stem: Exclusion bands apply to transmitter emission measurements while the transmitter is in standby.
explanation: Clause 4.3.2.1 says exclusion bands shall not be applied when measuring transmitters in standby. The 250% channel-width exclusion is for the transmitting case.

stem: Portable equipment in EN 301 489-1 Table 1 is subject to AC mains conducted emissions.
explanation: Table 1 marks AC mains conducted emissions, harmonics, flicker, and wired-network emissions as not applicable to portable use. Enclosure emissions of separately assessed ancillary equipment still apply.

stem: A fulfilment service provider, for Regulation (EU) 2019/1020, offers at least two of warehousing, packaging, addressing, and dispatching, without owning the goods.
explanation: Section 2.6 uses that definition. If no manufacturer, importer, or authorised representative is in the EU, that provider's traceability can be the one that has to appear.

stem: Series production has to stay in conformity after the first unit is assessed.
explanation: Section 2.3(k) requires the manufacturer to keep series production in conformity. Sample checks and a complaint register are part of the follow-up when the manufacturer judges them appropriate.

stem: An importer who believes the radio is not in conformity may still place it on the market if the price is reduced.
explanation: Section 2.5 says the importer does not place it on the market in that case. If the radio presents a risk, the importer informs the manufacturer and the market-surveillance authorities.

stem: Safety tests passed on the radio module are enough to close Article 3.1(a) for the final product.
explanation: REDCA TGN 01 §5.2 says a full safety assessment of the final product is required in most cases. Module safety results do not give that confidence.

stem: The wanted transmit signal may be watched with the monitoring receiver inside the immunity field.
explanation: Clauses 4.2.1 and 4.2.2 put external sources and monitoring equipment outside the test environment. An integral-antenna radio uses a link antenna inside the room and a shielded line out to the monitor.

stem: Narrowband spurious responses of a receiver during the conducted RF immunity test are counted as immunity failures.
explanation: Clause 9.5.2 says those discrete narrowband responses are disregarded. They are a radio selectivity effect, not the immunity result the test is scoring.

stem: A trade-fair transmitter demonstration also requires:
choices: An FCC grant for the demo
Contact with the relevant national spectrum authority
No sign, if the radio stays in a flight case
Only a CE mark painted on the booth
explanation: Section 1.6 says a transmitter demonstration means contacting the spectrum authority. The Article 9.2 sign, and measures against interference and risk, are still required.

stem: The manufacturer's name and address for traceability go:
choices: On the product, or on the packaging or an accompanying document if the product cannot carry them
explanation: Section 2.8(h) says the address printed on the declaration does not satisfy the product traceability duty. The product, the pack, or a document that goes with it has to carry the name and address.

stem: Instructions under the RED are written in:
choices: A language easily understood by end users, as the Member State determines
Pictograms with no words, in every case
explanation: The Guide requires a language end users can understand, as the Member State determines, and the text has to be clear. Frequency bands and power still belong in those instructions.

stem: Software that changes the radio's intended function in a way the first risk assessment did not foresee, raises the hazard, and is then made available:
choices: Makes the radio a new product
Takes the radio outside the RED
Leaves the original declaration in force with no review
explanation: Section 1.5 treats that combination as a substantial modification. A bugfix that does not affect compliance can stay in the maintenance category.

stem: The CE mark on radio equipment shows:
choices: That the manufacturer claims conformity with the applicable EU legislation, including the RED
That the EMCD declaration replaces Article 3.1(b)
That a notified body tested every unit
explanation: The Guide's manufacturer duties include affixing the CE mark, and the notified-body number when a module that uses a notified body was applied. The mark is the manufacturer's claim, not a test report.
